subject: houndeye
leg: control: Valve's own against the brief
label: houndeye, in the place of the game's models/houndeye.mdl

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/gman.mdl, models/scientist.mdl, models/hassassin.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked A, B, C, B where the asset was C, A, B, B: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: Outline matches the brief's words: a squat, rounded yellowish body on three legs, with a large dark round eye on the front (front and back views). In the sides the body is low and wide with a dorsal ridge of spines along the back, and the legs hang from its underside. No part sticks out or is missing in any of the ten views.

M2.reason: Measured 49.3 long, 33.5 wide, 44.7 tall against the brief's 49 long and 45 tall, a 0.6% difference, well inside 15%.

M3.reason: The brief asks for three thin legs, one large eye on the front, and striped and dappled hide. Three legs are there in the front view (left, centre, right) and the back view (three legs). The eye is one large dark round opening on the front, seen in the front, front-left and front-right views. The stripes are painted on the back. The brief names no claws, teeth or other small parts. Each leg ends in a foot that reads at game size.

M4.reason: The body is yellow-olive, the stripes teal and brown, and the pale belly is cream. The eye is dark with a reddish rim. This matches the brief's yellowish body and striped, dappled hide, with no region of the wrong colour or material in the views.

M5.reason: The teal and brown stripes run across the back and dorsal ridge (left, right and top views). The flanks carry a dappled, veined pattern (left and right views). The pale underside shows a fine vein pattern (below view). The detail is somewhat soft on the front in the front view, but it reads as the striped and dappled hide the brief asks for.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the rubric. In the line-up test the judges picked the asset once in four readings (reading 4) and missed it in the other three, so it was not caught twice or more and M6 is not reduced. Note: the line-up's other three models are a human (gman), a scientist and a hassassin, not creatures of the houndeye's kind, which makes the test easier than the rubric asks.

M7.reason: The eye faces front in the front view, the model is upright in the side views, and it stands on its three legs on the floor line (motion and attack sheets).

M8.reason: The checks report no errors. Triangles are 308, under the Half-Life median of 576 and well under twice it. Nothing visible is open, inside out or floating: the front eye is a dished dark surface with no background showing through, and the underside is pale. The underside's central dark mouth area is visible only from below, where the rubric does not count it.

C1.reason: In the run sheet (18 frames) and the attack sheet (59 frames) the body, legs and dorsal ridge stay together, and no part comes apart or sinks through the floor line. The legs move through the stride. In run frames 3, 5 and 8 the body sits above the floor line with the feet raised. Without the original's motion frames I cannot confirm that this matches the original's gait, so the score rests on the parts staying attached. The sonic blast is a behaviour, not a model item, and is not judged here.
